findings.claim: `$ZodNumberFormats` is referenced unqualified while every other core type in this block uses the `core.` namespace prefix; if the corresponding import was not added, this is a compile error.
findings.rationale: The surrounding code consistently uses `core.$ZodNumberFormatInternals`, `core.$ZodNumberParams`, etc. The hunk header (1193 -> 1194) suggests a line was added above, likely the import, but the import is not visible in this hunk, so I can't confirm. Medium confidence that it is fine, but worth verifying that `$ZodNumberFormats` is actually imported (and exported from core) rather than silently resolving to something else.

findings.claim: The runtime `ZodNumberFormat` constructor is still typed as the non-generic/default `core.$constructor<ZodNumberFormat>` (i.e. `Format = $ZodNumberFormats`), so it cannot preserve the concrete format of the value it constructs.
findings.rationale: Because the constructor value's type always widens to the full format union, every factory below now needs an unchecked assertion. Making the declared constructor type generic (or having `core._int`/`_float32`/... be typed to return the narrow format) would let the compiler verify the mapping instead of trusting the casts. Confident this is why the casts were needed; severity is design/maintainability, not a runtime bug.

findings.claim: The newly added `as ZodInt` / `as ZodFloat32` / ... assertions silence the only check that the declared literal format matches what the core `_int`/`_float32`/... helpers actually set at runtime.
findings.rationale: `int()` is now declared as `ZodNumberFormat<"safeint">`, but the assertion means nothing verifies that `core._int` really sets `format: "safeint"` (zod core has both `"safeint"` and `"int32"`). If any of the five helpers set a different format string, the declared type silently lies and downstream narrowing on `_zod.def.format` breaks with no compile error. Please double-check each literal against the corresponding `core._*` implementation. Reported once here; the same concern applies identically to the float32/float64/int32/uint32 casts.

findings.claim: Parameterizing `ZodNumberFormat` makes `ZodInt`, `ZodFloat32`, `ZodInt32`, etc. mutually non-assignable, which is a breaking type change for existing callers.
findings.rationale: Previously all five interfaces were structurally identical (`extends ZodNumberFormat {}`), so user code such as `const s: ZodFloat32 = z.float64()`, or arrays/ternaries mixing them, type-checked. With distinct `Format` arguments those now error or infer unions. This is likely the intended improvement, but it is a semver-visible type break worth calling out in release notes. Moderate confidence on the assignability consequence, depending on whether `Format` actually appears in `$ZodNumberFormatInternals`.
